title: code collector lane aborts wholesale on one unresolvable project
wanted_capability: Per-project error isolation in the code-source and published-knowledge lanes: with several [[projects]] configured, one project whose committed identity cannot resolve (resolve_committed_scope: no committed .bbox/config.toml at HEAD) fails the entire lane run, so healthy projects behind it never publish. Wanted: skip-and-report per project (like pending-onboard scopes on the daemon side) so one unadoptable repo cannot starve the rest of the fleet.
fallback_used: Producer-side config renderer gates the [[projects]] set on committed .bbox identity, so unresolvable repos never enter the lane.
evidence: observed 2026-08-16: 12-project config, 11 without committed .bbox, lane error starved the 1 healthy project
resolution_note: bbox-code-collector lanes (code-source, git-history, provenance, published-knowledge) now attempt every configured project and record per-project outcomes (LanePassOutcome): each failure is logged with its root and the pass continues. A pass where at least one project published keeps the lane on its normal cadence (only an all-projects failure drives the lane backoff); the one-shot `once` verdict still reports any failure. Same shape onboard_projects already had.
